First listed 2026-11-08 · episode or wrap

My Brutally Honest Thoughts About the AI Bubble.

Eisman organizes the AI boom into probability-weighted scenarios and five risks: capital intensity, power constraints, customer concentration, OpenAI fragility and weak model switching costs. He favors infrastructure suppliers while warning that an early major-model failure could hit the economy and multiple sectors. His distinctions between technology success and investor returns are useful. Several numerical premises require further verification; the EY interpretation is contradicted by the audit report and a quoted Oracle drawdown fails its own arithmetic.

YouTube · 2026-11-09 ↗Substack · 2026-11-08 ↗
Strong financing and moat framework, but risks are scenarios rather than realized calls. The Meta audit-work allegation is wrong; Oracle drawdown arithmetic is wrong. Negative quarterly cash flow is supported, while recession exposure, market-share claims and several headline totals remain unverified.

youtube-w1dRDj1QRks-c014 · analytical principle

If a software buyout starts with half debt and half equity and enterprise value halves while debt is unchanged, the equity is wiped out.

Right
Source · 15:19-16:12 ↗
SpeakerSteve Eisman
Stanceconditional
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

This conditional relationship follows from the stated assumptions; it does not establish that the assumptions hold empirically.

Conditional reasoning

Residual equity = max(50 - 50, 0) = 0. A public share-price decline alone does not establish this EV decline.

  • Initial EV = 100; debt = 50; equity = 50
  • EV subsequently falls to 50; debt unchanged; no cash additions or debt paydown

Assessment test: E = EV - D; test actual enterprise values and debt separately.

Evidence and assessment details

Attribution confidence: high. Assessment confidence: high. Thesis family: private_equity.
